newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon reports first Ebola death in capital.
newsitem.headline: Gabon reports first Ebola death in capital.

text.p: Gabon said on Monday one man had died of the lethal Ebola virus in its capital Libreville, the first such incident in a major African city.
A health ministry statement published in the government daily Union said several residents were believed to be infected.
Gabon has reported three Ebola epidemics since last year. But like in other previous cases of the haemorrhagic fever in Africa, the areas struck were far from large population centres.
Residents said the emergency unit of the Libreville Hospital Centre where the man died after admission on December 18 had been closed.
Ebola, which can kill as many as eight out of 10 people infected by the virus, causes fever and uncontrollable bleeding. It is transmitted through contact with contaminated body fluids.
The statement traced the latest outbreak to people who came into contact with Ebola victims in southern Gabon last October.

"Preliminary findings indicate that several people infected are now living in Libreville. Most have been identified but are not cooperating with authorities as we would have wanted," it said. Medical sources said last month that three people had
been admitted to hospital in Libreville after contracting Ebola from southern Ogooue-Ivindo province where the virus surfaced earlier in the year.
Ebola killed seven people in Oogue-Ivindo province in October and 13 died there in February.
It killed a nurse in South Africa last month but health officials there said there was no sign of the disease spreading. The nurse caught the disease from a Gabonese doctor she was treating.
Ebola, which originated in the jungles of Central Africa and has been linked in Gabon and Ivory Coast to apes or monkeys, killed 245 people in and around the Zairean town of Kikwit in 1995.
